content.title: About
content.content: Venison sausage is a meat sausage made from ground venison, often seasoned with salt, spices, and sometimes a small amount of fat. Venison has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and is considered a leaner meat compared to beef or pork.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Venison contains less fat and fewer calories than most other meats.
In traditional northern cuisines, venison sausage was prepared in cold climates for long‑term storage.
Venison is rich in iron and zinc, making it a valuable source of these minerals.
Venison sausage is often smoked, giving it a distinctive aroma and extending shelf life.
In some European regions it is known as “sausage de cerf.”

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Venison provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Venison sausage typically contains less saturated fat than pork or beef sausages.

items.title: High iron content
items.content: The iron in venison is readily absorbed and helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Vitamins B12, B6, and niacin support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Allergy to game meat
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to venison.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Like most sausages, it can be high in sodium; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Risk of contamination
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient cooking can allow bacterial growth.

items.title: Higher cost
items.content: Venison is usually more expensive than other meats, which may limit frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Venison sausage can be enjoyed cold as a snack, sliced thin for sandwiches, added to salads, pastas, or pan‑fried. It pairs well with mustard, cranberry sauce, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store venison sausage in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5–7 days. For longer storage freeze it at –18 °C; it will retain quality for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration.
